mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in FOMC communications
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, or the inflation surprise index (CPIAUCSL - lagged 1mo) is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals labor market resilience, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investor confidence improves.
regime_hint: Early in a labor market recovery phase
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive windows where PAYEMS > 200,000, the 60-day forward return is not statistically above the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 96.0 for two consecutive months, it indicates a strengthening supply-side momentum that is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, INDPRO > 96.0 fails to precede a positive 20-day forward return in more than 70% of instances (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained double-dip decline in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 216 for three consecutive months triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations of future disinflation erode equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 216 for two consecutive months and remains below for a third month
failure_condition: In 20 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for three consecutive months, it coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates rate cuts and liquidity expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.0% and remains below for two additional months
failure_condition: Across 10 such episodes, the 5-day forward return is not positive in more than 60% of cases (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 12-month moving averages for a month signals robust demand, which predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_12MA AND INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA in the same month
regime_hint: Dual momentum in consumer and business demand
failure_condition: In 20 such interaction windows, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in job openings (RSAFS) below 7.0 million for four consecutive months indicates softening labor market pressures, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During 10 such prolonged declines, the 20-day forward return is not persistently negative (rolling 30-day average p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) is negative for three consecutive months, it reflects supply-side weakness that precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 15 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
